situation:
You are to assume the role of guest marketing manager at BLACKPINE MOUNTAIN RESORT, a ski resort and mountain operator with a slopeside lodge that takes group and event bookings. The general manager (judge), hired last spring to lead the turnaround, has asked you to recommend how the resort should handle the resale market for its lift tickets, and to be ready to explain your reasoning.

Two thin snow years cost the resort much of its season pass base and forced a round of layoffs, and the crews who stayed took on extra work to keep the lifts running. Day tickets now appear on PASSLINE MARKETPLACE for well under the window price on every busy weekend, and group organizers choosing a lodge quote those resale prices back to the sales office. Some of the listings are staff comp tickets.

PASSLINE MARKETPLACE has offered to become the resort's official resale partner. Accepting that offer would give the resort a share of every resold ticket and a view of who is actually skiing on them. In exchange, PASSLINE sets the resale rules, and the email addresses of those buyers stay on the marketplace, so the resort could no longer send its own lodging and group packages to the people skiing its mountain.

Refusing the partnership leaves the resale market running with no share and no buyer information reaching the resort. It would also mean writing a work rule that voids a comp ticket once it is resold, which puts the general manager's new leadership in the position of policing the same crews who absorbed the layoffs, in the first winter those crews have been asked to trust it.

The general manager (judge) wants your recommendation, along with how such a work rule should be written and what the resort should say to the people it affects. The general manager (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
